title: The Negotiators and the Judge
subtitle: It is simple to denounce the evildoer, and far more difficult to understand them.

trails.title: Keyword
trails.description: Words are like stones beneath the river, catching the sunlight and guiding the current.

content.text:
Timekeeper,
    Regarding the slips of paper covered in unknown symbols that were tucked into Mr. Creius's letter—I spent some time analyzing them and eventually found relevant information in an old tome in the library.
    They follow an ancient and rarely used encryption method. I deciphered them and extracted several key fragments from the mass of meaningless character strings. I've transcribed them below:
 █ █∮Ω≈ Bereggrad Ψ∫λ∂∇█ █
 █ █∮Ω≈ List Ψ∫λ Amber Room ∂∇█ █
 █ █∮Ω≈ The Foundation Ψ∫λ Related ∂∇█ █
 █ █∮Ω≈ Secret Ψ∫λ Experiment ∂∇█ █
 █ █∮Ω≈ Urd Ψ∫λ∂∇█ █

items.text: The Negotiators and the Judge
A shallow valley separates the two armies.
The wind stirs seeds and dust. The warhorses grow restless under the eerie silence.

items.speaker: Zeno Officer I
items.text: I'll be damned. It's really him—Igor. After all this time, he just shows up here in Bereggrad? What's he trying to do, exactly?

items.speaker: Zeno Officer II
items.text: Whatever it is, he should do it soon so we can end him. I bet he wants to take his chances against us too.

items.speaker: Zeno Officer III
items.text: Not so fast. You know Igor parted ways with Manus Vindictae after the Antarctic operation.

items.speaker: Zeno Officer I
items.text: Are you on that traitor's side?

items.speaker: Zeno Officer II
items.text: He parted ways with us too!
The roar of broom engines on their return flight briefly drowns out the quarrel below.

items.speaker: Zeno Officer III
items.text: Alright, alright! Quit your bickering! The flight unit's back.

items.speaker: Zeno Officer III
items.text: It's all up to the commander now.
The commander lowers his telescope as he awaits the Flying Witches' news.
Lilya emerges from a whirl of dust stirred up by the Su-02ве.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Status?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: It's weird. It's Igor all right, Triple-As and all, but they didn't attack.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I flew low, too, even looked eye-to-eye with the soldiers, but they still held fire.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: As for the city, there's no signs of damage or Igor's men.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: His soldiers are all outside the city?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Yeah. Got his main force positioned along the main road to it. It's like he wants us to see him.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: He wants us to see him.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: If he wanted to stop our advance, capturing the city would've been the best bet.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: It's almost like he's welcoming us.
The commander raises his telescope again. This time, he spots a soldier riding out from Igor's army.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: What?
The messenger crosses the ground between the two forces, drawing closer to the cavalry. His rebel uniform causes quite a stir.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: That's—

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Calm yourself, Lieutenant. A rider must assess the terrain before he takes to a gallop.
The commander holds fire. The messenger reaches the cavalry formation and approaches the commander, escorted by a guard.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Commander Ivan Ivanovich. It's been a while.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: A long time indeed. What message do you bring, Ptolemy?
The messenger stares straight into the commander's eyes, intent on carrying out the mission entrusted to him by his father.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Admiral Igor wishes to talk with you and the Timekeeper, who's currently under your protection.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: There's something important he wants to discuss, about Bereggrad, the Don, and the Timekeeper's mission.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Igor has the information I need.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Seems he knows why you're here. Though this could be a ploy.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Hmm. It's too dangerous for the Timekeeper to meet Igor in person. They should speak via communication device instead.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They could easily have reached us through such devices. Given this message was brought by one of his most trusted subordinates ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I don't think it's negotiable.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What are your thoughts, Commander?
The commander finds himself the most unsure of his decision.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I want to know his purpose here, and him stationing outside the city does look like a gesture of goodwill.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: That said, I shouldn't meet him in private. Word will surely reach the Joint Committee.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I understand your concerns. But either way, I'll meet him.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper?!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I currently have almost no information on my mission. I'd like to know what he has to say, even if it's a lie.
The commander pauses to consider.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Our orders are to avoid confrontation. Accepting his request may be the way to do that. But ...

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Whether I join the meeting is your decision.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Me?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: The Committee will not question your motivations. If I attend, let it be by your bidding.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Then, if they question me, I will have my defense.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I see. I'll make the decision.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: But how can we ensure the safety of the Timekeeper and the others?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Meeting Igor, huh? Take me with you, Vertin. I'd like to hear what he's got to say.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Alright. I accept Igor's invitation, and I request the commander join me.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: To ensure the safety of both parties, I suggest we each bring our own bodyguards. Lilya will be ours.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: You could use another, Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, you're the only one who knows the details of the mission besides myself. One of us should stay in a safe place.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Relax. I'll bring Vertin back in one piece.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Understood. Please be careful, Timekeeper. I'll prepare a teleport disk for you.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: So it stands. I'll send a rider to Igor's messenger.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: We meet on the open plain, within striking distance of both sides.
In that space between armies, the air seems to tighten under the antagonistic stares of the opposing sides.
Tens of thousands of eyes are fixed on the few figures at the center of the valley. They walk toward each other across the open grassland.
Igor arrives first at the designated location and waits patiently.
He stands alone, not a single guard at his side.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I'm sorry that this is the way we meet again.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I feel the same, Igor. What did you want to talk about?
The rebel leader seems unfazed by his opponent's omission of rank.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: After the last "Storm," you helped Moldir escape Antarctica and avoid investigation by the Foundation. You have my thanks.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She provided us valuable support. I simply returned the favor.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: If that's all you got to say, then send a thank-you letter. Get to the point: what do you want?
Igor glances at Ivan, who watches in silence.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: There are some matters I want to clarify.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Where you want to start? From the first time you put on the Zeno uniform? Or from São Paulo?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: São Paulo. Let's start there.
To everyone's surprise, the admiral lets out the city's name. The sound of it almost stings.
The corner of Ivan's eye twitches.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Before I arrived in São Paulo, I struck a deal with the "dead" Arcana.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You communicated with Arcana after her death?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Yes. You witnessed the events in Antarctica. I trust there is no need to explain why I heard Her voice.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Death and resurrection are part of the myth She aimed to construct. I refused to become Her follower, but I desperately needed the reward only She could provide.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Arcana needed Urd to complete her resurrection ritual. What did you need?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: A true shelter.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: A "boon," a "hidden place," a "promise" from the Surpassing Excellence. She used many words for this little cube.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Is it familiar to you, Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The material's similar to the Tear of Comala.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The origin is the same, but their function is different.
Igor clenches his fist, and the black cube disappears.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Why make a deal with Arcana if just to avoid the "Storm"? The Foundation already provides you shelter.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: When you learn of Urd and the Amber Room, you will understand why I cannot trust the Foundation's promises. They have chosen a perilous path.
The name, mentioned too many times of late, plucks at a golden thread in her mind.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You know about the Amber Room too.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I know what led you here—Urd, Amber Room—the words appear together. But whoever gave you this intelligence likely knows little more than that.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Bereggrad is not a large city. But without guidance, you will never find the Amber Room, even if you turn it inside out.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Fortunately, its location is not a secret to me.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Because I was involved in it all.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: How much more do you know?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: No more questions. I am no longer bound by the Foundation's confidentiality rules. I can lead you directly to the answers.
Igor gives them space to consider the deal, then turns to the cavalry commander, who has not spoken a word.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Ivan, I know you care deeply for the Don. I admit some responsibility for the looting of the upstream villages.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Then it was you?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: It was Krutov.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Krutov? Hah. He or you, what difference is there? He betrayed Zeno at your side in São Paulo. He follows your orders.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Not since Antarctica. With the new era, Krutov has taken his own path. We have some differences of opinion.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The Manus deal was a one-off, but Krutov wants more.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: He believed our reward should be greater, that receiving only a small black cube was like pleasing a child with a toy.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: A traitor among traitors. Guess people do get what they deserve.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Sharp. You're right. I should've known that without Zeno, his desire would grow beyond my control. I will take the blame for his madness.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And for the Zeno soldiers you killed in São Paulo.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I will not deny it. And I will atone.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: But I must first stop what Krutov has done to the Don basin.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I trusted him—trained him under my command—but failed to see his inflating ambition. I did not snuff it when I had the chance.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: In the end, he built an army, from my soldiers and weapons, and from the Manus and other sources.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: In this era, our relationship has become rancorous. He hopes to snatch the "boon," and I hope to end this matter once and for all.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Then he and his bandit forces now belong to Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: He works with them as an ally, not a follower. He has not undergone the mask trial. Likely his arrogance is the reason.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Whether he has joined the Manus or not, it matters little.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: These differences of opinion among you rebels are the cause of the Don's suffering. If an ounce of duty is left in you, end it. Quickly.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I will launch an attack on Krutov when the time is right, but the battle will be hard-fought.
The admiral frankly admits the trouble his army is facing.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I'm sure you already have some information, but Krutov is more powerful than you think.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Zeno weapons, Manus troops, the backing of Don warlords—he has them all. My army alone cannot defeat him.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: That is why I ask your cooperation. With the Cavalry Corps, we will outnumber them. We will have the advantage.
Igor's words are like a shashka sunk into the mud, waiting for the other to pull it free.
Across the plain, tens of thousands of soldiers still face one another in tense silence.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Are you sure you know what you're doing?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I'm sure. And I hope I have proven my sincerity.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: This serves all parties. You will bring peace to the Don, and the Timekeeper will learn what she seeks of Urd.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: If you agree, everything will be settled within a week. You have my word.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The sunlight is fading, so is our time. I hope the deal can be made now.
